clue.text: Daily newspaper's takings

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a daily paper; with 'the' it reads THE FT
the possessive ending of newspaper's supplies the closing letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper's revenue, or what it took in on the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Daily newspaper's' as THE FT'S, the Financial Times being Britain's pink business daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings can be things taken unlawfully, so stealings or robberies fit the plural sense.

clue.text: Bent, like many an addict?

definitions.meaning: bent means curved like a hook
an addict is dependent on, or caught by, a drug

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both curved into a hook shape and addicted, unable to give something up.

clue.text: Trendy girl's about to be absorbed by most popular piece of music

indicators.note: to be absorbed by puts the first pieces inside the favourite

parts.note: fave is informal for favourite, the most popular
in means trendy, fashionable
gal is girl, so girl's gives GAL'S
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A trendy girl's tune is taken up by the top chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Mendelssohn's overture named after a sea cave in the Hebrides, off Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's Hebrides overture is popularly known by this name, after a sea cave in Scotland.

clue.text: Musical's reviewed at front of theatre programme

indicators.note: reviewed, looked at again and rethought, means the letters of Musical's are rearranged
front of means the first letter of theatre is used

explanation.surface: A musical's write-up appears at the front of a theatre programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast shown at the same time on radio and television, or several channels, is a programme.

clue.text: Amount of medicine doctor's initially expecting to keep the old well

indicators.note: to keep means the doctor's letters hold another piece within them

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor, so doctor's gives MO'S
egad is an old-fashioned exclamation, used like 'well!'

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of expecting is used

explanation.surface: A dispensing note about a doctor anticipating that an old well will be preserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amount of medicine' tempts one to take DOSE as wordplay, but the whole phrase is the definition; 'well' is an old exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A very large quantity of a drug taken at once is a huge dose, literally a mega-sized one.

clue.text: Not all current No.1s are covered by, say, boy band

indicators.note: are covered by puts those first letters inside the boy word

parts.note: a boy, for example, is male

indicators.note: No.1s means the first letters of not, all and current

explanation.surface: Not every current number one is a cover by some boy band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boy band' reads as pop music, but 'band' alone is the definition, a restraining ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A manacle is a metal band locked round the wrist, a fetter or handcuff.

clue.text: Writer making repeated attempts to get on line

indicators.note: repeated means the attempt word is given twice

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: An author tries again and again to get online.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was the Russian author of Dead Souls and The Overcoat.

clue.text: Endless fuss over small point

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, means the shortened word is turned upwards
endless means the last letter of the fuss word is dropped

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss

explanation.surface: Endless fuss is made over a trivial point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts TODO to TOD, and 'over' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a tiny spot or mark, a small point.

clue.text: What could make rocky areas wet?

definitions.text: What could make rocky areas wet?

indicators.note: rocky, unsteady, means the letters of areas and wet are jumbled

explanation.surface: A question about what soaks stony ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the sea's water wets rocks on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the ocean is what drenches rocky stretches of coastline.

clue.text: Nickname of Zurich banker embroiled in scam

indicators.note: embroiled in puts the banker inside the scam

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam
the gnomes of Zurich is a jibe at Swiss bankers

explanation.surface: A Swiss banker caught up in fraud is given a nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen is a distinguishing extra name, used loosely for a nickname or epithet.

clue.text: Food in the afternoon in most of France once, say?

definitions.text: Food in the afternoon in most of France once, say?

indicators.note: the second in places the meal inside the shortened country
most of means the last letter of the old country name is dropped

parts.note: Gaul is the old Roman name for the land of France
tea is a light afternoon meal

explanation.surface: A question about what is eaten in the afternoon across much of old France.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a rich cake is the sort of afternoon fare the French serve, and 'say?' flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich layered cream cake is a typical example of something eaten at afternoon tea.

clue.text: Regret trouble on the Internet coming back

indicators.note: on places the trouble after the turned word
coming back means the Internet word is read backwards

parts.note: the web is the Internet
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone regretting that online trouble keeps returning.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewail something is to lament or deeply regret it.

clue.text: Salad we locals ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of we locals are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Local people placing an order for salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage in dressing.

clue.text: Growth of flowers round tearoom overlooking lakes, a feature of Cumbria

indicators.note: round means the flower spike goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a spike is a flower head growing along a stem

indicators.note: overlooking, in a down clue, puts the tearoom above the lakes

parts.note: a cafe is a tearoom
L is the abbreviation for lake, so lakes gives LL

explanation.surface: A tourist scene: flowers growing round a tearoom above the lakes in Cumbria.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is a county in north-west England containing the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: England's highest mountain stands in the Lake District, making it a Cumbrian landmark.

clue.text: Theatre employee finds a celebrity reeling in shock

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the shock word

parts.note: to stagger is to shock or astound

indicators.note: reeling means a celebrity is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a celebrity is a big name

explanation.surface: A theatre worker finds that a star is staggered by a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reeling' turns the two words round, giving EMANA.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running the stage during a show is a member of the theatre's staff.

clue.text: Not interested in a course, along with other things one introduced

parts.note: a path is a course or route

indicators.note: introduced means one is put into the et cetera letters

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and other things
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone shows no interest in a course of study, among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means lacking interest or enthusiasm, indifferent.

clue.text: Showing greater determination, pilot goes without rest

indicators.note: goes without means the pilot word sits outside the rest word

parts.note: to steer is to pilot
to lie is to rest

explanation.surface: A determined pilot carries on without taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes without' reads as doing without, but means one word goes outside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means resolute and unyielding, so the comparative shows more resolve.

clue.text: Reportedly risk dental problem with European dish

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for risk is heard, not seen

parts.note: to stake is to risk or wager
tartar is hard deposit on teeth

explanation.surface: Someone risks a toothache while eating a continental meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw minced beef with onion and egg yolk is a classic restaurant dish.

clue.text: Attacked South African capital and leaderless settlement

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency, capital meaning money

indicators.note: leaderless means the first letter of the settlement word is dropped

parts.note: a town is a settlement

explanation.surface: A raid on South Africa's capital city and a headless settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a city, but here it means money, the rand.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to criticise or disparage them, an attack in words.

clue.text: Dearer to rent, we're told

indicators.note: we're told says the word for rent is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to hire is to rent

explanation.surface: Renting has become more expensive, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dearer costs more, carrying a higher price.

clue.text: Play safe with hammer

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to pan is to hammer or criticise severely

explanation.surface: An instruction to play it safe while using a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's stage work about the boy who never grows up is a famous play.

clue.text: Maker of wine to drink up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nip is a small drink

explanation.surface: Someone who makes wine invites us to drink up.
explanation.definitionFit: The grape variety is the fruit from which red and white wines are made.

clue.text: Stop getting on, restricted by strike

indicators.note: restricted by puts the age word within the strike word

parts.note: to hit is to strike
getting on in years means old

explanation.surface: A demand to stop, as an ageing worker is held back by industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word command is an interjection asking someone to halt or wait.

clue.text: In circulation, not a single book by great historian

indicators.note: in circulation, going round, means these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: not a single means no
great means big

explanation.surface: Not one copy of a great historian's book is in circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great' looks like part of the definition, but only 'historian' defines; 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon wrote The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, a celebrated historical work.

clue.text: University degree: good thing

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A university degree described as a good thing.
explanation.definitionFit: One's bag, in slang, is one's particular interest or speciality, one's thing.

clue.text: Altogether fair and square at the start

indicators.note: at the start places the square word before the fair word

parts.note: square means old-fashioned, unhip, as does out
right means fair, just

explanation.surface: Something done completely and honestly, from the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair and square' looks like a phrase meaning honest, but the words split: 'square' is OUT in the sense of unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means completely or entirely, as in winning a contest without qualification.

clue.text: I agree to visit outskirts of Belgian resort

indicators.note: to visit puts the agreement inside the outer letters
outskirts of means only the outer letters of Belgian are used

parts.note: righto is a casual way of saying I agree

explanation.surface: A traveller agrees to visit the edge of a Belgian holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside town on England's south coast; 'Belgian resort' misleads towards Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a seaside town in East Sussex long popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Bubbly husband always can get in Chambery on vacation

indicators.note: can get in puts these letters inside the emptied town name
on vacation means Chambery is emptied, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A lively husband can always get into the French town of Chambery while on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubbly person is lively and cheerful, full of good spirits.
